life_summary: Lyman Wight was born May 9, 1796, in Fairfield, New York, during the early years of American independence. He grew up in a rural area during a period of religious experimentation and frontier expansion. Wight was baptized into the Church of Christ by Oliver Cowdery on November 14, 1830, early in the movement's history. He married Harriet Benton on January 5, 1823, in Henrietta, New York, before his conversion and eventually married four wives in accordance with church polygamy doctrine, fathering eleven children. Wight was ordained to the high priesthood by Joseph Smith Jr. in June 1831, positioning him among the early ecclesiastical leaders of the rapidly growing movement.
church_summary: Wight served eleven missions as a member of the church and was ordained an apostle on April 8, 1841, to replace David W. Patten. Following Joseph Smith's death, Wight established separate communities in Texas, maintaining distinctive Latter-day Saint beliefs and practices. His followers built the first Latter-day Saint temple west of the Mississippi River in Zodiac, Texas, where members performed sealings, ordinations, washing and anointings, and adoption ceremonies. Wight's ministry emphasized community building and settlement establishment, and he was deeply involved in the tumultuous events of early church history in Missouri. His leadership demonstrated both the creativity and the sectarian divisions that characterized early Latter-day Saint expansion.
